feedback.problem: Write the complex number $z=3-2\text{i}$ in the form $r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ giving $\theta $ in radians to $3$ decimal places.
feedback.worked_solution:
To write $z$ in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{3}^{2}+(-2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{13}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $z$ lies in the fourth quadrant of the complex plane, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z) & =2\pi -|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =2\pi -|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{-2}{3})| \\  & =2\pi -|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(-\frac{2}{3})| \\  & ≈5.695.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=\sqrt{13}$ and $\theta =5.695$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get

$$
z=\sqrt{13}\,{\text{e}}^{5.695\,\text{i}}.
$$
